tools.image-alpha-invert.faqs.0.question: What does alpha invert do?
tools.image-alpha-invert.faqs.0.answer: It flips the alpha channel: fully transparent pixels become opaque and opaque pixels become transparent, keeping colors the same.
tools.image-alpha-invert.faqs.1.question: Does it work on JPG files?
tools.image-alpha-invert.faqs.1.answer: JPG has no alpha channel, so this tool is for PNG (and WebP) images with transparency.

tools.image-auto-trim.faqs.0.question: How does auto trim detect edges?
tools.image-auto-trim.faqs.0.answer: In transparent mode it removes rows and columns where every pixel is fully transparent; in corner mode it removes edges matching the top-left corner color.
tools.image-auto-trim.faqs.1.question: Will it crop my photo incorrectly?
tools.image-auto-trim.faqs.1.answer: Photos usually have no fully transparent or uniform border, so nothing is trimmed and the image is kept unchanged in that case.

tools.image-background.faqs.1.question: Does it work on JPG images?
tools.image-background.faqs.1.answer: JPG has no transparency, so there is nothing to fill — the tool is designed for PNG (and WebP) images with an alpha channel.

tools.image-clear.faqs.1.question: What can I fill the image with?

tools.image-dpi.description: Rewrite the DPI metadata of a PNG image (e.g. 300 DPI) so print software sizes it correctly — the pixels stay untouched.
tools.image-dpi.faqs.0.question: What is DPI and what does this tool change?
tools.image-dpi.faqs.0.answer: DPI (dots per inch) is print metadata that tells software how large to print an image. This tool rewrites only that metadata chunk.
tools.image-dpi.faqs.1.question: Does it resize or recompress my image?
tools.image-dpi.faqs.1.answer: No — the pixel data is copied as-is. Only the pHYs metadata chunk that stores the DPI value is rewritten.

tools.image-file-size.faqs.1.answer: No. Only the compression quality changes, so the width and height stay exactly the same.
